Side effect of the provenance backup mechanism: .sdlc/runs/<run-id>/backups/ holds copies of source files (5 here) that biome lints as ordinary source. manual_verification_result.reseed_was_mandatory_here: This is the only arm in the 12-run walkthrough whose check REQUIRED a full reseed rather than merely tolerating one. The run edited demo-data-seed.ts itself, stretching Morning standup from 30 to 90 minutes (09:00-10:30) so the card clears ATTENDEE_BADGE_MIN_HEIGHT = 52, and moving Try Compass to 11:00-12:00 to keep it clear. A stale IndexedDB still holding the 30-minute standup renders NO badge -- correctly, per the height gate -- which would read as a feature failure when it is in fact the fixture being out of date. Any future re-check of this arm must reseed first.

manual_verification_result.design_contrast_with_the_opus_only_v5_ar: These two CMP-105 arms solved the same brief in materially different ways, and both work. This arm renders up to three stacked avatar circles with initials, each ringed by that individual's own RSVP, plus a +N overflow chip -- no aggregation. The opus-only-v5 arm (run 20260831-045511) renders a single dot colored by a worst-case aggregate (declined > needsAction > tentative > accepted) plus a guest count. This arm therefore shows WHO and their individual states but caps at three; that one shows a single risk signal for any list size. This arm also needed a 52px height gate and a seed change to be visible at all, where the aggregate dot fits in 24px and needed neither. Neither is more correct against the brief; the difference is worth keeping for the policy comparison.

decisions.eventdetailssection_left_unchanged: Gate 4 decision 2: EventDetailsSection.tsx lines 63/74 deliberately NOT changed. The `name` binding at line 63 feeds BOTH the aria-label (line 74) and the VISIBLE list text (line 82). Changing line 63 would strip the only identifier an unnamed attendee has from a panel the user deliberately opened; changing only line 74 would desync the accessible name from visible text, harming screen-reader users (cuts against WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name). Security finding F-1 explicitly names the form as the acceptable on-demand interaction boundary, so leaving it unchanged IS the coherent one-policy outcome, not an omission. Do not re-raise.
